facts.one_liner: Borneo’s highest mountain rising above rainforest rich in orchids and pitcher plants.
facts.why_go: Kinabalu Park, inscribed in 2000 as one of Malaysia’s first UNESCO World Heritage Sites, protects the 4,095-metre Mount Kinabalu and one of the richest plant communities on Earth, including orchids, pitcher plants and Rafflesia. Climbers summit over two days.
facts.how_to_get_there: The park headquarters is about 2 hours by road from Kota Kinabalu.
facts.good_to_know: Climbing permits and mountain guides are mandatory; book well ahead.

facts.one_liner: Smoking volcanoes rising from a sea of sand at sunrise.
facts.why_go: Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park surrounds the Tengger caldera, a vast sea of volcanic sand from which Mount Bromo rises. At sunrise from viewpoints around Penanjakan, the steaming Bromo and the cone of Semeru, Java’s highest volcano, appear above the mist.
facts.how_to_get_there: Cemoro Lawang is the main base, about 3 hours by road from Surabaya or Malang.
facts.good_to_know: Volcanic activity can close areas—check alerts. Sunrise is very cold.

facts.one_liner: Sandstone cliffs and eucalyptus-blue valleys west of Sydney.
facts.why_go: Blue Mountains National Park is part of the Greater Blue Mountains UNESCO World Heritage Area. The blue haze comes from eucalyptus oil in the air. The Three Sisters rock formation at Echo Point in Katoomba is the icon, and walking tracks lead to waterfalls and lookouts.
facts.best_time: Year-round; spring and autumn are best for walking.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 2 hours by train from Sydney Central to Katoomba.
facts.good_to_know: Check track conditions and fire bans with NSW National Parks.

cards.name: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park

image.author: Norton Ip from Hong Kong
image.attribution: Photo: Norton Ip from Hong Kong, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
image.proof_notes: Commons file 'File:Dove Lake and Cradle Mountain (26200584572).jpg' (4896×3264) confirms Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair National Park; visually checked on contact sheet. desc: Dove Lake and Cradle Mountain, Tasmania.

facts.one_liner: A jagged peak above Dove Lake in Tasmania’s wilderness.
facts.why_go: Cradle Mountain-Lake St Clair is part of the Tasmanian Wilderness UNESCO World Heritage Area. The Dove Lake Circuit loops beneath Cradle Mountain, and the Overland Track runs south to Lake St Clair, Australia’s deepest lake. Wombats are often seen.
facts.best_time: December–March for warmer weather; snow is possible any time.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 2 hours by road from Launceston or Devonport.
facts.good_to_know: Shuttle buses run from the visitor centre to Dove Lake. Overland Track bookings are required in peak season.

facts.one_liner: New Zealand’s highest peak above glaciers and braided rivers.
facts.why_go: Aoraki / Mount Cook National Park holds New Zealand’s highest mountain, at 3,724 metres, and is part of the Te Wāhipounamu UNESCO World Heritage Area. The Hooker Valley Track leads over swing bridges to a glacier lake below Aoraki. The park is also part of an International Dark Sky Reserve.
facts.best_time: November–April for walking; winter for snow and clear skies.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 3 hours by road from Queenstown or 4 hours from Christchurch.
facts.good_to_know: Weather changes quickly and alpine tracks can close—check DOC alerts before you set out.

facts.one_liner: Golden beaches and clear bays along a famous coastal walk.
facts.why_go: Abel Tasman is New Zealand’s smallest national park, known for golden beaches and clear water. The Abel Tasman Coast Track is one of the country’s Great Walks, and water taxis and sea kayaks connect bays such as Anchorage.
facts.how_to_get_there: Marahau is the main gateway, about 1 hour by road from Nelson.
facts.good_to_know: Huts and campsites must be booked. Check tide times for estuary crossings.

facts.one_liner: Red rock gorges with waterfalls and swimming pools.
facts.why_go: Karijini, in the Hamersley Range, is known for its ancient red gorges. Fortescue Falls and Fern Pool in Dales Gorge are popular swimming spots.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 1.5 hours by road from Tom Price or Newman.
facts.good_to_know: Summer temperatures are extreme. Some gorges require experience.

facts.one_liner: Zimbabwe’s largest park, famous for its huge elephant herds.
facts.why_go: Hwange is Zimbabwe’s largest national park and is known for elephants. Waterholes draw herds in the dry season, and the park is also home to lions, painted dogs and many antelope.
facts.best_time: July–October, the dry season, when animals gather at waterholes.
facts.how_to_get_there: Main Camp is about 2 hours by road from Victoria Falls.
facts.good_to_know: Self-drivers should keep to roads and park rules.

facts.one_liner: Riverfront safaris with large elephant herds on the Chobe River.
facts.why_go: Chobe National Park in northern Botswana is known for its elephant population. Boat safaris on the Chobe River bring you close to elephants, hippos and crocodiles.
facts.how_to_get_there: Kasane is the gateway town, about 1.5 hours by road from Victoria Falls.
facts.good_to_know: Book boat safaris in advance during peak season.

facts.one_liner: Portugal’s only national park: granite mountains, waterfalls and old villages.
facts.why_go: Peneda-Gerês is Portugal’s only national park, in the north of the country along the Spanish border. Granite mountains hold waterfalls and pools, and stone villages such as Soajo and Lindoso keep old granaries.
facts.how_to_get_there: About 1.5 hours by road from Porto or Braga.
facts.good_to_know: Some routes need permits or are seasonally restricted; check park rules.
